# 01 - Data Exploration: Brent Oil Prices

This notebook performs initial Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) on the Brent oil price dataset.

Objectives:
- Load and inspect the data
- Visualize price trends
- Compute and analyze log returns
- Test for stationarity
- Observe volatility clustering
- Save cleaned data for modeling

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from statsmodels.tsa.stattools import adfuller, kpss

# Set plot style
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-darkgrid')
sns.set_palette("husl")

print("Libraries imported successfully!")

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('../data/raw/brent_oil_prices.csv', parse_dates=['Date'], dayfirst=True)
df = df.sort_values('Date').reset_index(drop=True)

print(f"Dataset shape: {df.shape}")
print(f"Date range: {df['Date'].min()} to {df['Date'].max()}")
print("\nFirst 5 rows:")
df.head()

# Check for missing values
print("Missing values:")
print(df.isnull().sum())

# Summary statistics
print("\nSummary statistics for Price:")
print(df['Price'].describe())

# Plot time series
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 6))
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['Price'], 'b-', alpha=0.7, linewidth=1)
plt.title('Brent Oil Prices (1987-2022)', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Date', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Price (USD/barrel)', fontsize=12)
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('../reports/figures/price_trend.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

# Compute log returns
df['log_return'] = np.log(df['Price'] / df['Price'].shift(1))

# Plot log returns distribution
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))

axes[0].hist(df['log_return'].dropna(), bins=50, color='steelblue', edgecolor='black', alpha=0.7)
axes[0].set_title('Distribution of Log Returns', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Log Return')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Frequency')
axes[0].axvline(x=0, color='red', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)

axes[1].plot(df['Date'], df['log_return'], 'g-', alpha=0.5, linewidth=0.8)
axes[1].set_title('Log Returns Over Time', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('Date')
axes[1].set_ylabel('Log Return')
axes[1].grid(alpha=0.3)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('../reports/figures/log_returns.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

# Stationarity tests
print("=" * 60)
print("STATIONARITY TESTS")
print("=" * 60)

# ADF Test (Null: series has a unit root - non-stationary)
result_adf = adfuller(df['Price'].dropna())
print(f"ADF Test p-value: {result_adf[1]:.4f}")
if result_adf[1] < 0.05:
    print("✅ ADF: Series is stationary (reject null)")
else:
    print("❌ ADF: Series is non-stationary (fail to reject null)")

# KPSS Test (Null: series is stationary)
result_kpss = kpss(df['Price'].dropna(), regression='c')
print(f"KPSS Test p-value: {result_kpss[1]:.4f}")
if result_kpss[1] < 0.05:
    print("❌ KPSS: Series is non-stationary (reject null)")
else:
    print("✅ KPSS: Series is stationary (fail to reject null)")

# Test on log returns (should be stationary)
result_adf_ret = adfuller(df['log_return'].dropna())
print(f"\nADF on Log Returns p-value: {result_adf_ret[1]:.4f}")
if result_adf_ret[1] < 0.05:
    print("✅ Log returns are stationary (expected)")

# Volatility clustering (absolute log returns)
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 5))
plt.plot(df['Date'], df['log_return'].abs(), 'r-', alpha=0.5, linewidth=0.8)
plt.title('Absolute Log Returns (Proxy for Volatility)', fontsize=14)
plt.xlabel('Date', fontsize=12)
plt.ylabel('Absolute Log Return', fontsize=12)
plt.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('../reports/figures/volatility.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.show()

print(f"Volatility (std of log returns): {df['log_return'].std():.4f}")
print(f"Max absolute log return: {df['log_return'].abs().max():.4f}")

# Save cleaned data
df_clean = df[['Date', 'Price']].copy()
df_clean.to_csv('../data/processed/cleaned_oil_prices.csv', index=False)
print("✅ Cleaned data saved to: data/processed/cleaned_oil_prices.csv")
print(f"Total records: {len(df_clean)}")
